The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Identify the oriented $S^3$ with the unit sphere in $\mathbb R^4$ by an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism and fix the standard height $h(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)=x_4$. Its only critical points are the two poles, and each regular level is a 2-sphere. A **Morse representative** of a smooth oriented knot $K$ is a knot ambient isotopic to $K$ on which $h$ has only nondegenerate critical points. Define the **bridge number** $b(K)$ as the minimum number of local maxima of $h$ on a Morse representative of $K$. The standard unknot is the oriented unit circle in a fixed coordinate 2-plane of $S^3$.

A **regular oriented diagram** is a projection of a smooth oriented knot with finitely many transverse double points, no other multiple points, and an over/under choice at each double point. A **crossing change** switches which branch is over at one chosen double point and leaves the projection and strand orientations unchanged. Define the **unknotting number** $u(K)$ as the minimum number of crossing changes needed to turn some regular diagram of a representative of $K$ into a diagram of the standard unknot. Both minima are taken in subsets of $\mathbb N$. The Morse-representative set is nonempty by the first well-definedness result below; under countable choice the regular-diagram existence result and the descending-diagram theorem below make the unknotting set nonempty. The bridge-number definition and the least-element argument in $\mathbb N$ require no choice; countable choice is used only to invoke the stated regular-projection supplier for $u(K)$.

Let $V_+$ and $V_-$ be the Seifert matrices obtained from their oriented disk-and-band surfaces. There are corresponding integral bases in which either $V_+=V_-$ or $V_+-V_-=\pm vv^T$ for some integral column vector $v$. In particular, $\operatorname{rank}(V_+-V_-)\le1$.

Let $A$ and $B$ be Hermitian forms on the same finite-dimensional complex vector space, and suppose that the linear map representing $A-B$ has rank at most one. Then $|\operatorname{sign}(A)-\operatorname{sign}(B)|\le 2$, where the signature is the number of positive eigenvalues minus the number of negative eigenvalues, with multiplicity and with zero eigenvalues omitted.

Define the **Levine–Tristram Hermitian matrix** by
$$H_\omega(V)=(1-\omega)V+(1-\bar\omega)V^T.$$
It is Hermitian because $V$ is real and $\bar\omega=\omega^{-1}$. Its signature is the number of positive eigenvalues minus the number of negative eigenvalues, both counted with multiplicity and with zero eigenvalues omitted. When $\Delta_K(\omega)\ne0$, define $\sigma_\omega(K)$ to be this signature. At a root $\omega_0\ne1$ of $\Delta_K$, define $\sigma_{\omega_0}(K)$ to be the arithmetic mean of the two one-sided limits of $\sigma_{e^{i\theta}}(K)$ as $\theta$ approaches an argument of $\omega_0$ from below and above. Assume full AC. For every $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$, changing an ordered basis by an integral unimodular congruence or changing a knot Seifert matrix by either elementary enlargement or reduction preserves the signature of $H_\omega$. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented embedded circle in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ be any ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ with Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $J_F$ be the matrix of the algebraic intersection form on $F$, with a transverse intersection of oriented curves $u,v$ counted positively exactly when their ordered tangent vectors form a positive basis of $TF$. Then $V-V^T=J_F$. The matrix $J_F$ is skew-symmetric and unimodular; when $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ is a standard handle basis, it is a direct sum of blocks $\begin{psmallmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{psmallmatrix}$.

For two successive knots in a crossing-change sequence, use the two corresponding bases from [F2]. If their Seifert matrix difference is $\pm vv^T$, their $H_{-1}$ difference is $\pm4vv^T$, of rank at most one; if the difference is zero, the same bound holds. By [F3], the absolute signature change is at most two. Step 1.1 identifies the signatures of these particular matrices with the knot invariants, regardless of which diagram surfaces occur at other stages.

By [F1], take a sequence of length $u(K)$ ending at the standard unknot. Its disk Seifert surface has an empty matrix and signature zero. Apply the estimate of step 2.1 to each consecutive pair and add the finitely many inequalities. The triangle inequality yields $|\sigma_{-1}(K)|\le2u(K)$, including a length-zero sequence. Together with step 1.1 this proves both claims.
